S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

patient_info.stressor: Jason and his wife moved from their long-kept Connecticut house to a smaller condominium closer to medical offices, the library, and their adult children, requiring him to sort decades of teaching files, tools, garden records, and model railway materials. During the move, his usual methodical habits shifted into persistent intrusive concerns about misplacing important items or making irreversible decisions, and he responded with repeated checking, list-making, and mental retracing that went beyond practical organization. The pattern caused mild impairment: unpacking stalled, library tutoring preparation took longer, and his wife noticed he was avoiding enjoyable tasks until he felt things had been verified enough. He brought it up during a routine primary-care visit, and his physician referred him for psychiatric evaluation when Jason described feeling unable to stop the cycle despite recognizing it was excessive.

S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.
S065.manifestation: I keep getting these nagging thoughts that I may have thrown away something important from my old teaching files or put a needed tool in the wrong box, and even when I tell myself it's unlikely, the thought comes back and makes it hard to settle.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: What brought me in is that I find myself checking the same boxes, lists, and condo drawers over and over before I can move on, even though I know perfectly well I already looked and my wife is waiting for me to just leave it be.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: Unpacking the condo has taken much longer than it should, and I’ve been putting off my library tutoring preparation and hobbies because I feel I can’t move on until things are verified enough.
